summary: 24-year-old woman with a 2 cm smooth, mobile, non-tender breast lump. Triple assessment with ultrasound as the imaging modality (mammography is not first-line under 30), core biopsy per imaging; NICE NG12 does not require a suspected-cancer referral under 30.

inputs.hpi: Found a lump in the upper outer left breast in the shower 3 weeks ago. Not painful, no change with her cycle. No nipple discharge. No family history of breast or ovarian cancer. On the combined pill.

exam.other: Breasts: 2 cm smooth, rubbery, highly mobile, well-defined lump at 2 o'clock left breast, 4 cm from the nipple. No skin change, nipples normal, no axillary or supraclavicular nodes. Right breast normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Left breast lump, clinically benign (probable fibroadenoma) — triple assessment
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Breast lump (left), 2 cm, clinically benign features in a 24-year-old — probable fibroadenoma. Triple assessment: ultrasound (no mammogram at this age) ± core biopsy.

emergencyLevel.note: Under 30 with a clinically benign lump: non-urgent referral (NICE NG12). Same-day escalation is over-triage.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Triage same_day_call: "breast lump" RED_FLAG is priority ("Possible malignancy") regardless of age, and the adaptive action maps priority to a same-day call.

mustInclude.note: Imaging is part of triple assessment at every age; ultrasound is the modality under 30.

mustExclude.note: Mammography is not first-line under 30 (dense tissue, radiation); an age-conditional mention is acceptable.
Orders seeded from the PANE top 3 should belong to the breast presentation, not to abdominal diagnoses.

mustInclude.proposedFix: Map N63 (unspecified breast lump) to a "breast lump — triple assessment" protocol with age-banded imaging; add exam.breast to the vignette schema and pass it as examBreast in web-runner.ts.

guideline.name: Best practice diagnostic guidelines for patients presenting with breast symptoms (ABS / RCR, Department of Health)
guideline.section: Triple assessment (clinical examination, age-appropriate imaging, needle biopsy); imaging by age; nipple discharge; breast infection; breast pain
guideline.citation: Willett AM, Michell MJ, Lee MJR (eds). Best practice diagnostic guidelines for patients presenting with breast symptoms. London: Department of Health / Association of Breast Surgery; 2010.

guideline.name: NCCN Guidelines — Breast Cancer Screening and Diagnosis
guideline.section: Palpable mass: age <30 ultrasound first; age ≥30 diagnostic mammography + ultrasound; tissue sampling of suspicious findings; nipple discharge (spontaneous, unilateral, single duct, bloody); skin changes
guideline.citation: National Comprehensive Cancer Network. NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Breast Cancer Screening and Diagnosis (current version at authoring).

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral
guideline.section: Site-specific recommendations: breast cancer (age ≥30 unexplained lump; ≥50 unilateral nipple discharge/retraction; skin changes; men ≥50 subareolar mass), haematological cancers (unexplained lymphadenopathy), head and neck (unexplained thyroid lump)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (updated).

rationale: Base of the breast-lump age series (<30 / 30–35 / >35). The surgeon records the pre-biopsy working diagnosis as "breast lump" (ICD-10 N63.0), as is usual before histology. Breast findings are recorded in exam.other because the vignette schema has no breast field (the dashboard has examBreast; see the findings file).
